newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria budget deficit tops '96 target by 21 pct.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria budget deficit tops '96 target by 21 pct.

text.p: Bulgaria's central government budget deficit topped the 1996 annual target by 21.1 percent, rising to 97.7 billion levs on November 17, Finance Ministry figures showed.
The deficit rose by 9.7 billion levs between October 31 and November 17 as expenditure rose by 24.3 billion levs while revenue increased by 14.5 billion levs.
BULGARIA BUDGET DEFICIT, bln levs NOV 17 OCT 31
"The deficit rise was due mainly to large interest payments on domestic debt in the first half of the month," a Finance Ministry official said, declining to elaborate.
No further details were immediately available.
The Bulgarian National Bank's central interest rate is now set at 15 percent monthly or 180 percent annually.
The Finance Ministry recently started to cover maturity payments on government securities with rollover issues of treasury paper.

Bulgaria's parliament in July revised the budget in a move to meet high foreign and domestic debt payments and to keep structural reform on track, raising the deficit target from 58.3 billion levs to 80.7 billion levs or 4.9 percent of gross domestic product.
Some 52.6 percent of total expenditure in the revised annual budget or 231 billion levs were allocated to cover interest payments on foreign and domestic debt.

Government debt rose to 668.3 billion levs at the end of October from 640.6 billion levs a month earlier and 345.4 billion levs at the end of last year. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569; 981 4145
